summary: Eldorado National Forest lookout with a 1912 steel tower, a 1915 replacement after windthrow, a 1958 dismantling bid, and a 1965 CL-100 cab on a 30-foot tower.

facts.design: CL-100 14 by 14 foot metal live-in cab on a 30-foot steel tower

events.note: October 27, 1911 notice: government constructing a house as permanent headquarters for a lookout man on the peak
Steel tower of 60 feet per May 18 and August 3, 1912 notices (ordered, then completed); an October 3, 1912 report says 62 feet with a concrete base
R.F. Kelley assigned to the lookout post (June 5, 1914)
Tower toppled by February 1915 winds; May 29, 1915 notice says a more substantial structure will replace it; a new steel tower was being erected by July 10, 1915
Orin Murdock sent to the station in April 1931
June 6, 1932: Mr. and Mrs. R.O. Murdock moved to Bald Mountain for the summer; Mr. Murdock in charge of the station
October 7, 1938 item names Lookout Orrie Murdock on Bald Mountain
October 30, 1958 notice: Forest Service sealed bids for the lookout and for dismantling the existing tower
Register gives 1965 for the present CL-100 cab on a 30-foot steel tower
August 2, 1982 Mountain Democrat item: live-in staffing from May to November, Sunday to Thursday
300-gallon water tank stolen sometime during the winter; theft discovered May 15, 1983

corrections.why: The register says the present cab sits on a 30-foot steel tower (9.1 m), and a 1982 Mountain Democrat item says 32 feet (9.8 m). The record's 50-foot figure (15.2 m) does not appear in any source read.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1912 steel tower (60 or 62 feet) and the 1965 CL-100 cab on a 30-foot tower are different structures. The 1958 bid to dismantle the existing tower is undated in its outcome; the sources do not say whether a tower stood between 1958 and 1965.
Two 1912 notices give 60 feet and an October 1912 report gives 62 feet; these describe the earlier tower, not the present cab.

notes_for_editor: Record height of 15.2 m (50 feet) is not supported; the register gives a 30-foot steel tower and a 1982 item says 32 feet. Nearly all history comes from dated newspaper items quoted on the Forest Lookouts page, not checked against the original papers. The 1911 to 1983 items were re-read in full on the page, including the 1931-1983 entries; the 1982 item names its subject as Delma and the fire specialist as Dwain Schrader. Current staffing, rental and access are unknown. Two web searches found no Eldorado source on this lookout, and the Forest Service page turned up was about Big Hill. The 1958 bid may have covered the 1912 tower; whether a tower stood on the site before 1965 is not stated. The 1982 staffing is recorded as staffed, with no current information.
